deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a heavily corrected draft of an epistemological passage from Riemann's natural-philosophy notes. It continues the previous page, which asks: (1) When is our conception of the world true? Answer: when the connection of our representations corresponds to the connection of things. (2) What is given? Answer: sensations and their fusion into images.

The argument on this page runs as follows.
(a) The tail of the preceding sentence: spatial apprehension does not rest on the given representations alone. It also involves either laws of representation formed in earliest childhood (following Herbart's genetic psychology) or innate forms of intuition (Kant). Riemann leaves the alternative open.
(b) 'As is well known', the qualities of the features of sensible things lie only in our sensation and do not exist outside us. These are colour, smell, taste, warmth or cold; several of the items are struck through. This is the classical primary/secondary quality distinction.
(c) Therefore the connection of things can be recognised only from quantitative relations. These are the spatial and temporal relations of sensible things, and the degree of difference of their features in intensity and quality: intensity ratios and quality differences.
(d) From the observed connection of these magnitude-relations, the general laws of nature that express the connection of things are to be found.
(e) Hence the task of explaining nature is formulated, marked III: 'From the connection of appearances, to find the connection of things.'
(f) The representation of sensible things in spatial and temporal relations is indeed what one already finds when one starts deliberate reflection on nature. But this representation is itself already a result of our apprehension of what the senses give.

The next page is a cleaner redraft of the same passage, renumbered 'II. Woraus soll der Zusammenhang der Dinge gefunden werden?' It confirms the reading.

In modern terms, the only quasi-formal content is a structural-realist thesis. A true world-picture requires that the relational structure among representations match the relational structure among things, roughly a homomorphism or isomorphism of relational systems. Only quantitative magnitude-relations are invariant enough to carry that structure. This is philosophy of science, not mathematics; nothing is computed.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there is no mathematics. Philosophically, the claim that qualities 'do not exist outside us' is asserted as 'bekanntlich' (well known) without argument. That is standard for the period (Locke, Helmholtz's sign theory), not a slip.

results.what: Truth of a world-picture defined as correspondence between the connection of representations and the connection of things; only quantitative (spatial, temporal, intensive) relations carry this correspondence.
results.modern_name: Structural realism / Helmholtz-Hertz picture (Bild) theory of scientific knowledge
results.usually_credited_to: Helmholtz (sign theory, 1850s-1867); Hertz (Bild theory, Prinzipien der Mechanik, 1894); structural realism later (Poincaré, Russell, Worrall 1989)

results.what: Primary/secondary quality distinction: colour, smell, taste, warmth are merely subjective.
Task of natural explanation: from the connection of appearances to find the connection of things.
results.modern_name: Programme of theoretical natural science / inference to underlying laws
results.usually_credited_to: General 19th-century Herbartian/Kantian epistemology; Riemann's philosophical fragments were partly published by Weber/Dedekind in the Gesammelte Werke (1876)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely epistemological and contains no mathematics. Riemann's Herbartian natural-philosophy fragments are known, and versions of this material appear in the Werke's philosophical fragments. The picture-theory formulation anticipates Hertz's Bild theory somewhat, but Riemann's interest in such ideas is already recognised. This is a draft variant of an adjacent clean page.
transcription_corrections: The right-margin insertion read as 'die veranlassend zu diesen Verhältnissen {+der Sinnendinge+}' is almost certainly 'die räumlichen und zeitlichen Verhältnisse der Sinnendinge'. This matches the next page's 'die räumlichen und zeitlichen Verhältnisse der Raumdinge'.

The final paragraph, given as 'Die [-Vorstellung-] von ... Sinnendingen ... veranlassenden zu deren zeitlichen Verhältnissen ist nun zwar [-Voraussetzung-], und wir können absichtlichen Nachdenkens über die Natur vorhanden', should read roughly: 'Die Vorstellung von [der Existenz von] Sinnendingen in räumlichen und zeitlichen Verhältnissen ist nun zwar [-Voraussetzung-], was wir beim absichtlichen Nachdenken über die Natur vorfinden.' Compare the next page.
Line 3 likely reads 'in frühester Kindheit gebildeten Vorstellungs-[gesetze]' rather than 'in früher Kindheit'.
The deleted list items among the qualities likely include 'Farbe', 'Klang/Ton' and 'Geruch'. Only 'Geschmack' and 'Wärme oder Kälte' clearly survive undeleted.
The marginal addition reads '; ausser uns nicht Existirendes', which matches the next page; the '[?]' can be dropped.

In the 'Aus ...' sentence, the right-margin text reads '... Zusammenhang dieser Grössenverhältnisse' following struck 'den Gesetzen, welche den'. The surviving sense is: 'Aus dem beobachteten Zusammenhang dieser Grössenverhältnisse sollen die allgemeinen Naturgesetze ... gefunden werden.'
The 'III' at the left margin is a section number. On the next page the passage is renumbered as II.
